\abstract{\textbf{Motivation:} Long reads can be assigned to the parental haplotype they were sequenced from, but current phasers do so through heterozygous variants called against a single linear reference. Reads in regions where the caller finds no heterozygous variant stay unphased, and in collapsed duplications the differences between paralogous copies mimic heterozygous variants, phasing reads, and whole blocks, in the wrong orientation. Haplotype-resolved analyses that use the reads themselves need as many reads as possible phased, and phased correctly.\\
\textbf{Results:} We present pgphase, which phases reads at the known alleles of a pangenome graph, observed directly in the reads' graph alignments, together with the sample's own heterozygous variants found in its linear alignments. A single expectation-maximization learns how reliable each site is, and phase blocks are joined only where several reads support the join. On HG002 PacBio HiFi reads, with each read's parent of origin as truth on eight chromosomes, three of them held out during development, pgphase phased 99.1\% of 2.6 million phaseable reads correctly, compared with 94.4\% for the best of HiPhase, LongPhase, WhatsHap and longcallD. It left 6.1 times fewer reads misphased or unphased than the best alternative, and made 58 switch errors against 105 for the next best tool.\\
\textbf{Availability and implementation:} pgphase is free software under the MIT license, available at \url{https://github.com/kokyriakidis/pgphase}.}
